text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein follows Israeli-Palestinian efforts to conclude a deal over an Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron.

- In a meeting of the Jordan Rift Valley (JRV) committee Crown Prince says the region "will witness soon a real breakthrough" and emphasises "the need to move from the planning stage to developmental process in the Valley."
- Rise in prices of stock in the Amman Financial Market on optimism in the Middle East peace process and Iraq's pledge to continue to supply Jordan with cheap oil.
- An economic delegation heads to Baghdad on Wednesday to continue talks on a 1997 trade accord.
- Coming elections of the lawyers union are expected to witness a showdown between Pan-Arabists and Islamists.
- Cabinet discusses the government's decision to sell a 26 percent stake in the state owned telecommunicatons body to an international strategic investor by end of 1997.
- Jordanian-Israeli talks held to deepen commercial ties, ease flow of goods and advance plans to develop the Jordan Rift Valley along their two borders.
- Israeli pledge to ease trade and movement of people across border crossings with Jordan.
- Prince outlines efforts to advance the Middle East peace process.
